case_title: Baljinder Kaur v. State of Punjab
high_court_outcome: Confirmed conviction of the appellant and Pritam Singh
neutral_facts: The accused, Baljinder Kaur, was the sister-in-law of the deceased, Sharanjit Kaur. The deceased married Pritam Singh in January 1997. After two months of marriage, the deceased informed her father and the mediator about the husband and his family members demanding dowry and harassing her. The accused demanded a gold bangle as dowry two months after the marriage. The deceased returned to her father's house due to the dowry demand, but was sent back to her husband's house after one month. She returned to her father's house again with the same demand. Two days before her death, the accused took her back to the matrimonial house. The deceased was found in critical condition and died of poisoning on the way to the hospital. The police registered an FIR under Section 304B IPC, and the accused were charged with dowry death. The prosecution argued that the accused subjected the deceased to cruelty and harassment for dowry demands soon before her death. The accused denied the allegations, and the trial court convicted all four accused under Section 304B IPC. The High Court confirmed the conviction of the appellant and Pritam Singh while acquitting the father-in-law and mother-in-law.
